expo.name: Demo Store
expo.//scheme: The app's own URL scheme. expo-router needs one for deep links, and it is also what a payment provider would need in order to return a shopper to the app rather than to a web page - see the return-URL note in the README.
expo.//appId: Deliberately generic. example.com is reserved by IANA for exactly this, so a sample app id can never collide with a real owner - and prebuild otherwise invents one from whoever is logged in on the machine that ran it, which puts a person's name in a public repo and in every build. Replace it with your own reverse-DNS before publishing anywhere; Google Play refuses com.example.

android.//usesCleartextTraffic: The store API is reached over plain http on the LAN, and Android has blocked cleartext by default since API 28 - so without this a development build fails every request to http://192.168.x.x with a bare 'Network request failed' and nothing pointing at the cause. It is a development affordance only: a real deployment reaches the API over https and does not need it.

expo.//plugins-fast-sse: Referenced by path, not by package name, and that is not a style choice. react-native-fast-sse ships no app.plugin.js at its root, so naming the bare package makes Expo load the package's runtime entry as a config plugin - which crashes `expo export` and `expo prebuild` with an ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION about requiring an ES module. The built plugin is at plugin/build. What it does: adds UIBackgroundModes 'fetch', forces the iOS deployment target to 15.1 (Nitro's minimum), and sets newArchEnabled on Android. All three are needed for a long-lived native SSE socket. It is a Nitro module either way, so this app needs a development build and will not run in Expo Go.
